citation.title: Neural Networks for Postprocessing Ensemble Weather Forecasts

topic: Distributional-regression neural networks trained with Gaussian CRPS for postprocessing ensemble 2-m temperature forecasts at German stations
own_question: Can neural networks with auxiliary predictors and station embeddings improve probabilistic postprocessing relative to EMOS, boosting, and QRF baselines?
actual_method_and_evidence: The networks have no hidden layer or one hidden layer. They predict Gaussian mean and standard deviation from ensemble summary statistics and use learned station embeddings. Training uses a closed-form CRPS loss, early stopping on a 20% hold-out, and averaging over 10 network instances. Models were trained on 2015 or on 2007–15 data and evaluated on 2016. Table 2 reports a mean CRPS of 0.82 for 2015 training and 0.78 for 2007–15 training, compared with 0.85 and 0.80 for EMOS-loc-bst. Feature importance was assessed by permutation. This is a weather application, not a plasma application.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Proper scoring rules such as CRPS can serve as training losses for neural networks that output parametric predictive distributions.
claim_checks.qualification: Shown for a Gaussian 2-m temperature target only. It is not evidence for CES nowcasting.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Offline 48-h-lead forecast postprocessing. It does not address current-report nowcasting or report arrival timing.
validation_if_relevant: Temporal hold-out, with 2016 as the test year. Diebold–Mariano tests were combined with Benjamini–Hochberg correction.
forbidden_inferences: Do not infer that NN postprocessing results transfer to KSTAR CES or to BES/ECEI data
Do not infer anything about real-time fusion control
Do not treat this paper as plasma prior work
Do not claim that CRPS is required by our study
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional citation, at most, as cross-domain background on CRPS-trained probabilistic regression and temporal held-out evaluation. It is not needed for the intro framing.
